system_description.narrative_title: Europe's socio-economic strain: political unrest and industrial retreat
system_description.narrative_summary: A wave of domestic political unrest in Spain driven by housing costs and a looming election is colliding with a broader industrial retrenchment in Germany and across Europe as major automakers pause investment and production. These domestic strains expose supply‑chain vulnerabilities and accelerate strategic shifts (including ties to Chinese manufacturers), feeding back into politics, financial stability and EU institutional debates. The window shows an interlinked crisis of competitiveness, social discontent and corporate repositioning.
system_description.scope: Within the boundary: Western European political dynamics (notably Spain and Germany), domestic socio‑economic drivers (housing crisis, cost of living, labor mobilization), industrial actors and decisions (automakers, steel industry, major manufacturers), supply‑chain and competitiveness indicators, and EU institutions/policy signals (ECB, fiscal borrowing). Flows include protests → policy responses → electoral outcomes; corporate investment/production decisions → employment and regional economies; international competition (China) → industrial strategy.
system_description.super_system: Global political‑economy (international trade, investment flows, geopolitics and global supply chains)
adjacent_subsystems: EU institutions and monetary/fiscal policy (ECB, EU budget rules, EU industrial policy)
Global automotive and manufacturing supply chains (China–Europe trade, steel markets)
Labor movements and domestic politics (unions, elections, social policy)
Financial stability and banking sector shocks (regional bank crises, market confidence)

variables.name: Domestic political unrest
variables.description: Level of mass protest activity, strikes and civil disorder within the domestic polity measured by frequency and intensity.

variables.name: Housing affordability
variables.description: Ratio of housing costs (rents and prices) to median household income and the accessibility of housing markets.

variables.name: Cost-of-living pressure
variables.description: Degree to which inflation and essential expenditures outpace wages, producing financial strain on households.

variables.name: Labor mobilization rate
variables.description: Speed and frequency at which organized labor actions (strikes, coordinated stoppages, mass actions) are initiated over time.

variables.name: Electoral volatility
variables.description: Variation in public voting intentions and the probability of significant shifts in electoral outcomes between cycles.

variables.name: Public trust in governance
variables.description: Population confidence in public authorities and perceived legitimacy of policy-makers and public institutions.

variables.name: Industrial investment rate
variables.description: Flow of new capital expenditures in the manufacturing and heavy-industry sectors per unit time.

variables.name: Manufacturing output rate
variables.description: Volume of manufactured goods produced per time period relative to installed capacity.

variables.name: Corporate restructuring rate
variables.description: Rate at which firms change production footprints, workforce size, ownership arrangements or strategic focus.

variables.name: Supply-chain vulnerability
variables.description: Degree of exposure of production processes to disruption from concentrated suppliers, chokepoints or single-source inputs.

variables.name: Import dependency ratio
variables.description: Share of key intermediate and final goods sourced from external markets relative to domestic supply capacity.

variables.name: Industrial competitiveness gap
variables.description: Relative disadvantage in unit costs, productivity, technology adoption and market access versus external competitors.

variables.name: Fiscal borrowing pressure
variables.description: Magnitude of government borrowing needs and budgetary strain relative to fiscal space and financing capacity.

variables.name: Financial system risk
variables.description: Vulnerability of financial markets and intermediaries to shocks, defaults and contagion across sectors.

variables.name: Policy adjustment rate
variables.description: Speed at which public policy instruments (regulation, subsidies, fiscal measures) are changed in response to socio-economic stress.

variables.name: Supply-source shift rate
variables.description: Rate at which firms reconfigure sourcing and supplier relationships toward alternative external or domestic sources.

catalysts.title: Spain snap election campaign
catalysts.description: A snap election and intensified campaign season in Spain tied to recent housing decrees, likely to reshape political dynamics and policy priorities.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "General strikes to paralyze Spain... ahead of election campaign"; "Spain approves one of housing decrees that triggered snap election".

catalysts.title: Ongoing Spanish general-strike wave
catalysts.description: A series of coordinated general strikes and labor actions in Spain is likely to continue, sustaining public disruption and political pressure.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Millions of Spaniards stage first general strike in 14 years"; "Spain Hit by General Strike as Cost of Living Takes Center Stage Ahead of Elections."

catalysts.title: Mercedes halts German investments
catalysts.description: Mercedes-Benz's announced halt to all future German investments initiates a sustained withdrawal of capital and potential plant closures in Germany.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Mercedes-Benz to halt ‘all future investments’ in Germany"; "Mercedes-Benz halts German investments as plant closures loom."

catalysts.title: VW production cut and worker escalation risk
catalysts.description: Volkswagen's decision to drop a major production program at its main plant risks escalation with workers and near-term production reductions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "VW drops 'Gamechanger' production at main plant, risking escalation with workers."

catalysts.title: Expansion of Chinese auto/steel presence in Europe
catalysts.description: Chinese automakers and industrial players expanding in Europe (including supply, investment and sales) will shift competition and sourcing dynamics across sectors.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Chinese carmakers offer lifeline to Europe’s struggling steel industry"; "Europe’s struggle to compete with China ramps up."

catalysts.title: Implementation of Spain housing decrees
catalysts.description: Rollout and enforcement of recently approved housing decrees in Spain will directly affect affordability, landlord investment incentives and political debate.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Spain approves one of housing decrees that triggered snap election."

catalysts.title: Corporate supply‑chain diversification push
catalysts.description: Corporate responses to reported vulnerabilities — shifting suppliers, adding redundancy or reshoring — will alter sourcing patterns across key goods sectors.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "A Quarter of Key Goods Vulnerable to Supply Disruptions, Study Finds"; logistics and corporate cost management stories.

catalysts.title: Near-record German borrowing for 2027
catalysts.description: Germany's planned near-record new borrowing for 2027 and associated budget deals will increase fiscal strain and prompt policy trade-offs.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Germany set for near-record new borrowing in 2027 after difficult budget deal."
